hero_subtitle: Explore how Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council manages public money. Reform UK is the largest party (15/38 seats, 39%) after the 7 May 2026 election but the council sits in NOC. Full transparency data coming soon.
publisher_bio: This website was created by Tom Pickup, Reform UK county councillor for Padiham and Burnley West and Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care at Lancashire County Council. He is also parish councillor for Clowbridge with Dunnockshaw. Tom builds transparency tools that make public spending data easier to check.
publisher_titles: County Councillor for Padiham and Burnley West
Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care, Lancashire County Council
Parish Councillor for Clowbridge with Dunnockshaw
publisher_quote: It's your money. The more people understand where it goes, the better.

political_control.tenure_note: Reform UK minority administration since the 20 May 2026 AGM. Cllr George Finch (Reform, also Reform leader at Warwickshire CC) Leader. NOC: Reform 16, Labour 10, Conservative 9, Green 3 (38 seats across 19 two-member wards; 20 needed, Reform 4 short). A 1 July 2026 vacancy resolved to Reform by 2 July 2026 (mechanism not stated on the council's pages). The 2026/27 budget was set by the outgoing Labour administration and inherited by Reform; a £3.5m draft deficit was closed to a £10,756 surplus. Stock-holding HRA council.
political_control.source: nuneatonandbedworth.gov.uk 'Who Controls the Council' page + per-ward councillor index (both read 2 July 2026) + General Fund Revenue Budget 2026/27 (Full Council 25 Feb 2026).

doge_context.political_control: Reform UK largest party — 15/38 seats (39%) at the 7 May 2026 election. NOC. 2nd party Labour.

spend_triangulation.note: Transparency gross = £256.3M across every class in the published corpus. Procurement-paid (discretionary third-party payments) = £254.4M. Non-procurement rows: internal transfers to pension fund / in-house provider / wholly-owned subsidiary (£1.9M) — all excluded from third-party-supplier forensic analyses. Net revenue budget figures (where published) are smaller again because they net capital, grants received, and reserves movements — transparency totals include all of these.

procurement_paid.note: Discretionary third-party supplier payments — the real procurement footprint.

internal_transfer.note: Council's own pension fund, in-house provider arm, or wholly-owned subsidiary. Money from commissioner to provider within the authority boundary.
